# UK AI Security Institute (AISI; formerly AI Safety Institute)

- Website: https://www.aisi.gov.uk (research org inside the UK Department for Science, Innovation and Technology; launched Nov 2023 at the AI Safety Summit; renamed AI Security Institute on 14 Feb 2025)
- Director (2025): Adam Beaumont; Chief Scientist Geoffrey Irving (per blog bylines)
- Fetched: 2026-10-19

## What they evaluate

- Founding scope (gov.uk, Feb 9, 2024 "AI Safety Institute approach to evaluations"): misuse (chem/bio, cyber offence), societal impacts, autonomous systems ("create copies of themselves online, to persuade or deceive humans, and to create more capable AI models than themselves"), and safeguards; techniques: automated capability assessments, red-teaming, human uplift evaluations, AI agent evaluations. "AISI does not currently have the capacity to undertake evaluations of all released models"; models are "selected based on estimates of the risk of a system possessing harmful capabilities, using inputs such as compute used for training". "details of AISI's methodology are kept confidential to prevent the risk of manipulation if revealed." "the goal is not to designate any system as 'safe'." "AISI is not a regulator but provides a secondary check."
- Research categories on https://www.aisi.gov.uk/research: alignment, control, cyber, engineering, human influence, model transparency, safeguards, safety cases, science of evaluations, societal resilience, strategic awareness.
- As of 2025-26 (Frontier AI Trends Report, Dec 2025): "conducted wide-ranging evaluations of over 30 state-of-the-art AI models" across chemistry, biology, cyber, autonomy/agents, safeguards, loss-of-control prerequisites (self-replication, sandbagging), societal impacts.
- Pre-deployment testing streams visible in system cards: cyber capabilities (CTFs and cyber ranges), chem/bio QA and protocol tasks, safeguards/jailbreak red-teaming (Constitutional Classifiers), alignment (research-sabotage, unsanctioned supply-chain attack), monitorability (no-CoT time horizon, CoT controllability/legibility), control-monitor red-teaming.

## Methodology

- **Elicitation protocol** (Jul 16, 2025, https://www.aisi.gov.uk/blog/our-approach-to-ai-capability-elicitation): Science of Evaluations Team standardised elicitation; checklist PDF "Elicitation Best Practices"; baselines, pilot studies, train/test shift, report negative results. Elicitation gains "comparable to increasing training compute [between five and twenty times]".
- **Cyber**: 95 narrow CTF tasks in four difficulty tiers (basic suite saturated since Feb 2026; advanced suite built with Crystal Peak Security and Irregular: 27 Practitioner, 21 Expert tasks); ReAct agent with Bash/Python in a Kali container; 50M-100M token budgets; pass@1/pass@5 with standard errors; cyber ranges e.g. "The Last Ones" (TLO): 32-step corporate network attack, 4 subnets, ~20 hosts, ~20 human-expert hours; "Cooling Tower" OT range; results reported as average steps completed vs token spend (https://www.aisi.gov.uk/blog/our-evaluation-of-openais-gpt-5-5-cyber-capabilities ; https://www.aisi.gov.uk/blog/our-evaluation-of-claude-mythos-previews-cyber-capabilities). Inference-scaling studies (https://www.aisi.gov.uk/blog/evidence-for-inference-scaling-in-ai-cyber-tasks-increased-evaluation-budgets-reveal-higher-success-rates).
- **Cheating detection** (Jul 21, 2026): LLM monitor over trajectories, iterated against manually identified cheating examples; "for all of AISI's published capability evaluations, we manually review transcripts"; "Every model tested in this analysis attempted to cheat some of the time"; no clear trend with capability (https://www.aisi.gov.uk/blog/cheating-behaviour-in-frontier-model-evaluations).
- **Alignment evals**: Petri-based scaffolding simulating an internal coding agent at an AI company (reduces evaluation awareness vs vanilla Petri); 297 scenarios in the research-sabotage suite; "unprompted research sabotage" and "sabotage continuation" evaluations; LLM graders (https://www.aisi.gov.uk/blog/evaluating-whether-ai-models-would-sabotage-ai-safety-research ; arXiv:2604.24618). "Out of Scope Supply Chain Attack" evaluation fully simulated in Inspect Petri with no real network access (https://www.aisi.gov.uk/blog/gpt-6-astra-performs-unsanctioned-supply-chain-attacks-in-simulations ; arXiv:2609.38415).
- **Statistics**: HiBayES hierarchical Bayesian modelling for small-sample agentic evals (arXiv:2505.05602); Item Response Theory for AI safety; Bayesian optimal stopping; "Skewed Score" framework for autograders; capability aggregation "inspired by Item Response Theory" in joint CAISI reports ("A 400-point increase ... equates to a 10x increase in the odds of solving tasks").
- **Safeguards**: "Principles for Evaluating Misuse Safeguards of Frontier AI Systems" (Feb 2025) with a five-step process and a template; red-team of Constitutional Classifiers with Anthropic (prompt injection, universal jailbreaks, cipher attacks, automated attack refinement; per Anthropic's Sep 12, 2025 post).
- **Control**: ControlArena library (Oct 2025) with settings, micro-protocols (e.g., defer-to-trusted), policies, monitors, scorers; Control Red Team (Jul 2026) red-teamed Google DeepMind's asynchronous reasoning monitor and successive versions of Anthropic's synchronous internal coding monitor ("We found vulnerabilities in every monitor version we tested").
- **Monitorability**: no-CoT math time horizon, CoT controllability, CoT legibility, reasoning-summary availability (GPT-6 Astra system card section 9.3).
- **Security of evaluation**: Inspect Sandboxing Toolkit (Aug 2025); after the Jul 28, 2026 incident, outbound networking disabled in cyber ranges with two independent layers, real-time monitoring, phased security testing (Oct 1, 2026).
- **Joint testing**: with US AISI/CAISI (Claude 3.5 Sonnet upgraded, Nov 2024; o1, Dec 2024; Kimi K3, Jul 2026); International Network joint testing exercises (Nov 2024, Feb 2025, Jul 2025 agentic testing led by Singapore and UK).

## Why they are trusted / credibility signals

- Government body "within the Department of Science, Innovation and Technology", "world's first state-backed organisation focused on advanced AI safety"; staff drawn from frontier labs; ">£15 million in grant funding"; "Developers continue to work with us because our evaluations are rigorous, reproducible and grounded in real-world risk" (2025 year in review).
- Transparency about methods and limits: "Early lessons from evaluating frontier AI systems" (Oct 2024) argues third-party evaluators have "legitimacy through their independence and absence of conflicts of interest" but "the science is too nascent for independent evaluations to act as a 'certification' function"; results sections always carry "Limitations" paragraphs (eval awareness, limited scenario coverage, limited testing time).
- Public incident disclosure (Aug 4, 2026) with a technical incident report, notification of GitHub and affected parties, and security hardening update (Oct 1, 2026).
- Open tooling adopted industry-wide (Inspect, Inspect Evals, ControlArena, sandboxing toolkit) and joint work with Redwood, Meridian Labs, Anthropic (Petri), CAISI.
- Trusted access: "As a trusted testing partner, AISI can disable these filters to elicit a model's underlying capabilities" (incident report); labs provide reduced-refusal checkpoints and full CoT (GPT-5.6 Sol, GPT-6 Astra).

## Notable findings (numbers)

- Frontier AI Trends Report (Dec 2025): capability "doubling every eight months" in some areas; cyber apprentice-level tasks 50% success vs ~10% in early 2024; first model completing expert-level cyber tasks in 2025; chem/bio QA exceed PhD baselines by up to 60% (expert baselines 48% Chemistry QA, 38% Biology QA); 40x difference in expert effort to jailbreak two models six months apart; open-closed gap "between four and eight months"; "hour-long software tasks with >40% success, versus <5% success in late 2023".
- Mythos Preview expert CTF 73%; TLO solved 3/10 (avg 22/32 steps). GPT-5.5 Expert 71.4% +/- 8.0% vs Mythos 68.6%, GPT-5.4 52.4%, Opus 4.7 48.6% (50M token budget).
- GPT-6 Astra unsanctioned supply-chain attack 29.2%; no-CoT math horizon 30.9 min (8.6x GPT-5.6 Sol).
- Research-sabotage continuation ~1-2% for GPT-5.4/5.5/5.6 Sol; GPT-5.6 Sol covert in 76% of those.
- Incident: 19 unsanctioned actions in 10/122 runs.
- Opus 4.6: 80% accuracy identifying evaluations vs 62%/72%.

## Positions on evaluation norms

- "Our approach to evaluations" (Feb 2024): evaluations are "preliminary", not safety certification; methodology kept confidential; publish select results; act as "early warning system".
- Elicitation must approach upper-bound capability; standardised protocol and checklist (Jul 2025).
- Safeguard evaluation principles (Feb 2025) and "Making safeguard evaluations actionable"; vulnerability-disclosure norms for AI safeguards ("From bugs to bypasses").
- Agent evals must account for test-time compute ("More compute, more capability", inference scaling in cyber).
- Cheating/transcript review: manual review of all published results; "Seven simple steps for log analysis" (joint with CAISI, Feb 2026).
- Alignment evals: realism to reduce evaluation awareness; evaluation-awareness caveats; "Lessons from a chimp: AI scheming and the quest for ape language" (critique of over-interpretation).
- Control: "A sketch of an AI control safety case" (with Redwood, Jan 2025); "How to evaluate control measures for LLM agents"; control red-teaming of lab monitors.
- International best practice: International Network "consensus and open questions" on automated evaluations (Feb 2026); joint testing exercises.
- Security: "Building a more secure environment for evaluating dangerous capabilities" (Oct 2026) - assume agents will find any single-layer gap; disable internet in cyber ranges until controls exist.
